Processor power. I'm not familiar with amd but for Intel i recommend core I series. Personally I would go with an I5 or I7 but i3 can be fine depending on what he does. Resolution of the screen as well. 1920x1080 is the lowest you might want so he can watch 1080p stuff on it at full resolution. For ram I would recommend at least 4 gigs. Hard drives can also be replaced if need be. A regular hdd should be fine and he can replace it with an ssd later if he wants. Dell or hp both make decent laptops. I have not used acer or others but have heard good things. Not sure about the keyboard. It could be possible to order one and get a U.S. keyboard.

Depends entirely on what you want from a laptop.

Go with an i5 with no graphics card for general office work, opt for a bigger hard-drive and less specs from a higher quality brand/sturdy build. Don't get anything that isn't a modern processor, as the older ones are not worth what they are being sold for.

Depends on what he is actually going to be using it for. Is this for business or personal? Does he play games(high level games) and would he want to on the laptop?

If his needs are email, FB, spreadsheets, and power point, I would focus on durability over specs. Better to have it work after a drop, then spend money of high end processing when it will not be used.

Just my two cents.
